label: main season
summary: E1 is direct evidence: the survey team observed and photographed an object that looked like EO. The national criteria provide no technical survey, so the defined hazardous area with this target proceeds to clearance. E2 is additional indirect evidence of past fighting; it does not negate E1. This is a recommendation for sign-off, not a final decision.
flags: Area record describes the land as 100% forest, while E1 places the observed object at the edge of a pasture; verify this location/land-use discrepancy during follow-up.

checks.detail: Every item of the evidence log is in the register.
The national criteria provide no technical survey, so clearance takes its place; evidence to target: E1, E2.

E1.quote: The survey team saw an object that looked like explosive ordnance on the ground at the edge of the pasture.
E1.note: The survey team directly observed and documented an apparent EO item, which is direct evidence; its own observation is reliability class 1.

E2.quote: there was fighting on the ridge in the area around 1999
E2.note: The report of past fighting suggests possible contamination but does not confirm EO; the local woodcutter is an informant familiar with the area, though his statement does not establish EO presence.
